html:
On 10 September 1880 the Makoko, king of the Teke or Tio kingdom on the lower Congo river, signed a treaty with Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza placing his lands under French protection.

The Tio kingdom had for centuries controlled trade on Malebo Pool, where the river becomes navigable inland. Brazza was racing Henry Morton Stanley, who was working for Leopold II on the south bank. The treaty gave France a claim to the north bank, where Brazza founded a post that became Brazzaville.

The French parliament ratified it in 1882, and it was recognised at the Berlin Conference. The river at the Pool still divides the two Congos, French-speaking capitals facing each other across the water.
sum: On 10 September 1880 the Makoko, king of the Teke or Tio kingdom on the lower Congo river, signed a treaty with Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza placing his lands under French protection.
